logline: A brooding Mumbai DCP with a genius for criminal psychology and a talent for crossing lines pursues a series of complex murders in this Indian remake of the BBC's Luther.

bollymeter.basis: Ajay Devgn's performance is the reason to watch; Film Companion and other critics found the adaptation too close to a scene-for-scene Luther copy with insufficient cultural rewriting to justify its existence, landing a 6.7 on IMDb.

seasons.review_body: Released simultaneously across all six episodes on Disney+ Hotstar on 4 March 2022, Rudra: The Edge of Darkness is an official remake of the BBC series Luther, transplanted to Mumbai with Ajay Devgn playing DCP Rudraveer Singh opposite Raashii Khanna's morally complex foil. Critical reception split along predictable lines: those unfamiliar with Luther found a watchable, atmospheric crime thriller propelled by Devgn's brooding screen presence; those who knew the original found Film Companion's verdict - steadfastly derivative in its vision - difficult to argue with. The show's central weakness is the lack of cultural translation: it copies Luther's architecture without bending the psychology to fit the Indian setting. IMDb audiences rated it 6.7, reflecting a middle ground between engaged newcomers and disappointed Luther fans.

episode_reviews.title: Khooni Khel
episode_reviews.review_body: Rudra: The Edge of Darkness Season 1 Episode 1 'Khooni Khel' released March 4, 2022 on Disney+ Hotstar as the premiere of the 6-episode official Indian adaptation of the BBC series Luther. IMDb audience scored the series 6.7. Film Companion called it 'steadfastly derivative in its vision'; The Quint found it 'a breath of fresh air' and was excited to see more of Ajay Devgn in web shows. The premiere introduces DCP Rudraveer Singh via a psychological confrontation that mirrors Luther's pilot structure closely: the detective reads the primary antagonist's body language before a word is spoken and builds a trap from inference rather than evidence. Ajay Devgn commands the frame in these scenes; his presence is the episode's strongest argument for the adaptation's existence. The Mumbai texture is present as atmosphere but insufficiently rewritten to generate the cultural specificity that would separate Rudra from its source material.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes DCP Rudra's methods - psychological acuity deployed without institutional patience - and introduces the season's primary antagonist with a first-scene revelation that mirrors Luther's pilot beat for beat. Ajay Devgn commands the frame; the Mumbai textures, though underutilised, at least give the procedural a local pulse.
episode_reviews.the_moment: Rudra reading the suspect's body language before a word is spoken - Devgn's best moment of the opener, built from intensity rather than dialogue.

episode_reviews.title: Antim Sach
episode_reviews.review_body: Rudra: The Edge of Darkness Season 1 Episode 6 'Antim Sach' released March 4, 2022 on Disney+ Hotstar as the finale of the 6-episode series. IMDb audience scored the series 6.7. Film Companion called it 'steadfastly derivative'; The Quint found it dramatic and was excited to see more of Devgn in web format. The finale resolves the primary case and includes a rooftop confrontation that is visually the season's most ambitious sequence - the moment where Rudra comes closest to being its own show rather than a Luther copy. Ajay Devgn and Raashii Khanna carry the confrontation scenes with genuine commitment; the writing's failure to adapt the cultural architecture of the BBC original leaves the emotional stakes the episode reaches for under-built. The ending gestures toward a second season that was never announced.
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The finale resolves Rudra's primary case and gestures toward a second season without fully earning the emotional weight it reaches for. Devgn and Khanna carry the confrontation scenes; the writing lets them down by staying too close to the Luther template rather than finding a conclusion specific to these characters in this city.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The rooftop standoff - the season's most visually ambitious sequence, and the closest Rudra comes to being its own show.
